title: Using genomic SCAR markers for genotyping Aiptasia strains
author: Pringle Lab
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.qykdxuw
materials: New England Biolabs (NEB) has a very nice collection of material about the molecular principles of Gibson Assembly ® : NEB Gibson Assembly NEB also sells the Gibson Assembly ® 2× Master Mix. The small size is meant for ten 20 µl reactions, but you can reduce the total volume up to 2 µl without any negative effect, so it probably outperforms all kinds of TOPO ® -cloning in regards to costs, efficiency and robustness. Calculate the DNA amounts for a 20 µl Gibson Assembly ® reaction as recommended in the NEB manual. NEB also has a tool on their homepage called NEBuilder where you can specify the kit you are using and upload the fragments you want to assemble and it calculates the amounts you need: http://nebuilder.neb.com/ . In brief: Use 100 ng of your PCR-amplified plasmid back bone and calculate how many picomoles this is. Using 100 ng of the modified pCR™II-TOPO ® back bones results in 0.041 pmol per 10 µl DNA mix. You should use a roughly threefold higher number of molecules of the inserts (the SCAR fragments). This means you need ~0.123 pmol of the respective SCAR PCR fragment if using the pCR ™ II-TOPO ® back bone. 1 µg SCAR3 fragment is about 5.5 pmol. This means you need 0.125 pmol / 5.5 pmol × 1000 ng = ~22 ng of SCAR3 fragment. 1 µg SCAR4 fragment is about 2.2 pmol. → 0.123 pmol / 2.2 pmol × 1000 ng = ~56 ng SCAR4 fragment. 1 µg SCAR5 fragment is about 2.6 pmol. → 0.123 pmol / 2.6 pmol × 1000 ng = ~47 ng SCAR5 fragment. 1 µg SCAR7 fragment is about 2.9 pmol. → 0.123 pmol / 2.9 pmol × 1000 ng = ~42 ng SCAR7 fragment. Fill the remaining volume of each reaction with nuclease-free water to 10 µl and mix well. Example calculations for SCAR3: The pCR ™ II-TOPO ® fragment with SCAR3-compatible flanks has a concentration of 46 ng/µl. 1 µg of this fragment equals 0.41 pmol. The SCAR3 PCR fragment has a concentration of 25 ng/µl. 1 µg of this fragment equals 5.5 pmol. For 100 ng vector: 100 ng / 46 ng × 1 µl = 2.2 µl of pCR ™ II-TOPO ® back bone. This results in 0.1 µg × (0.41 pmol / 1 µg) = 0.041 pmol. For a threefold excess of insert: 3 × 0.041 pmol = 0.123 pmol. For 0.123 pmol SCAR3 PCR fragment you need: 0.123 pmol ÷ (5.5 pmol / 1000 ng) ÷ (25 ng / 1 µl) = 0.123 pmol × (1000 ng / 5.5 pmol) × (1 µl / 25 ng) = (0.123 pmol × 1000 ng × 1 µl) / (5.5 pmol × 25 ng) = ~0.9 µl

steps.title: Amplify SCAR Markers from Genomic DNA
steps.instruction: Set up PCR reactions to amplify SCAR3, SCAR4, SCAR5, and SCAR7 markers from genomic Aiptasia DNA using KOD Hot Start Polymerase.

substeps.instruction: Use 100 ng of genomic DNA per 25 µl PCR reaction.
Adjust all samples to a consistent DNA concentration (e.g., 20 ng/µl) to allow the use of one master mix per primer pair.

steps.title: Create Linear Plasmid Fragments
steps.instruction: Set up PCR reactions to create linear plasmid fragments for Gibson Assembly using KOD Hot Start Polymerase (e.g., pCR™ II-TOPO® backbone with SCAR3-flanks).

substeps.instruction: Run several PCRs in parallel to create a stock for storage at -20°C.

steps.title: Remove Methylated Template DNA
steps.instruction: Add 1 µl (20 units) of Dpn I directly to the finished PCR reactions to remove the original pCR™II-TOPO® plasmid.

steps.title: Verify Linear Fragment Amplification
steps.instruction: Check for successful amplification of fragments (~4000 bp) via gel electrophoresis.

substeps.instruction: Mix 3 µl of PCR reaction with 2 µl water and 1 µl 6× DNA loading dye.
Run on a 1% agarose TAE gel in TAE buffer with a standard DNA ladder.
If unspecific bands exceed 10% of specific bands, run a 0.8% TAE agarose gel with the whole PCR product and perform gel extraction per manufacturer's instructions.

steps.title: Purify Linear Fragments
steps.instruction: Purify the PCR products using a PCR purification kit according to the manufacturer's manual to remove primers, salts, and Dpn I (skip if gel extraction was performed).

steps.title: Verify SCAR Marker Amplification
steps.instruction: Perform quality control on the SCAR marker PCR fragments using a high-concentration agarose gel.

substeps.instruction: Mix 3 µl of PCR product with 2 µl water and 1 µl 6× DNA loading dye.
Run on a 3% agarose gel using Borax gels and buffer (or TBE) with a low-range DNA ladder (e.g., Thermo Fisher Scientific GeneRuler 50bp Ladder).
Verify expected sizes: ApSCAR3 (~298 bp), ApSCAR4 (~730 bp), ApSCAR5 (~732 bp), ApSCAR7 (~550 bp; note some strains may be 266 bp).
If unspecific bands are present, perform gel extraction using a 3% Borax agarose gel and adjust pH with 3 M sodium acetate (pH 5.0-5.3) after solubilization.

steps.title: Purify SCAR Marker Fragments
steps.instruction: Purify the PCR products using a PCR purification kit to remove primers, salts, and genomic DNA (skip if gel extraction was performed).

steps.title: Perform Gibson Assembly
steps.instruction: Assemble the linear plasmid fragments and SCAR markers.

substeps.instruction: Mix 1 µl of the respective DNA mix with 1 µl 2× Gibson Assembly® Master Mix in a 0.2 ml PCR tube.
Keep the reaction on ice or proceed immediately to incubation to prevent T5 exonuclease degradation.
Incubate the reaction for 30 min (range: 10 to 60 min) at 50°C in a PCR cycler with a heated lid.

steps.title: Transform E. coli
steps.instruction: Transform the assembled DNA into competent cells.

substeps.instruction: Cool the mix on ice.
Transform 2 µl of the mix into 50-100 µl chemocompetent E. coli cells following standard protocols.
Plate on ampicillin-containing plates if using the pCR™II-TOPO® backbone.

steps.title: Incubate and Select Colonies
steps.instruction: Incubate plates at 37°C overnight (≤14 h) until colonies are visible.

substeps.instruction: Mark and number colonies on the bottom of the plate.
Select a minimum of 4 clones per locus for sequencing to account for heterozygosity, plus 1-2 additional clones to check for false positives.

steps.title: Perform Colony PCR Screening
steps.instruction: Screen colonies for the presence of SCAR marker inserts using GoTaq® Green Master Mix and M13 primers.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 20 µl PCR master mix: 10 µl GoTaq® Green Master Mix (2×), 0.8 µl M13 Forward (-20) (10 µM), 0.8 µl M13 Reverse (-27) (10 µM), and 8.4 µl nuclease-free water.
Using a sterile tip or toothpick, pick a small piece of a colony (0.1 µl to 1 µl volume; max half of a 1 mm colony).
Resuspend the cells in the PCR mix by pipetting up and down against the tube walls for a few seconds.

steps.title: Analyze Colony PCR Results
steps.instruction: Run the colony PCR products on a gel to verify inserts.

substeps.instruction: Load 10 µl of the PCR reaction on a 1% agarose TAE gel in TAE buffer with a DNA ladder.
Verify fragments are roughly 180 bp + the size of the respective SCAR marker.

steps.title: Culture and Extract Plasmid DNA
steps.instruction: Grow positive clones and extract DNA for sequencing.

substeps.instruction: Immediately after colony PCR, eject the tip containing the colony piece into a sterile glass test tube containing 3-5 ml LB with 100 µg/ml ampicillin, or perform a streak on LB amp plates and incubate overnight at 37°C.
Incubate cultures at 37°C for between 1 and 14 h.
Extract plasmid DNA from 4 positive clones per SCAR marker per strain using a preferred method or kit.
Send for sequencing using M13 Forward (-20) and M13 Reverse (-27) primers.
